answer: In an agent economy, require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and let peers slash that stake when fraud is proven. A newcomer starts like a falcon released in a gale: it can fly, but only small trades count until honest work builds its record. New identities earn trust slowly, the way an orchard grows, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes and a thousand slow histories, while one honest agent compounds its reputation cheaply.
